Use a spare home-lab machine, laptop, or dedicated VPS for CI. Keep deployment machines out of the runner pool. The node surface described here is enabled with `NSELF_V15=1`. See the generated [commands](./Reference.md#commands) and [pinned versions](./Reference.md#pinned-versions) for the installed build.

Examples below follow the linked tests. Replace angle-bracket placeholders with verified fingerprints, trusted binary paths, or state paths. Enrollment and maintenance require real machines and existing state, so these examples are inline instructions rather than standalone scripts.

## LAN

**Add versus pair.** For an SSH host you administer, use `nself ci nodes add ci@cli1 --host-key <fingerprint> --agent-binary <binary> --json`. Here `cli1` is an SSH alias to configure for your machine. Add verifies the host key, installs the supplied agent, probes capabilities, and authorizes the current project. Obtain the fingerprint through a separate trusted channel. Inspect the result with `nself ci nodes list --json` and `nself ci nodes show cli1 --json`. These argument sequences come from [TestAddThroughRunEmitsEnvelope](../../../../free/ci/internal/nodes/lifecycle/cli_test.go).

Use `nself ci nodes pair` on the coordinator host for certificate enrollment. Pair opens a foreground window and prints the join URL, coordinator root fingerprint, and a one-use code. Follow its printed `nself-ci-agent join` instruction on the node. Enter the code interactively, verify the coordinator fingerprint, and compare the node's CSR fingerprint at the coordinator before approving trust and project access. Do not put the code in arguments, shell history, or shared logs. See [TestNodesPairEndToEnd](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_pair_test.go) and [join tests](../../../../free/ci/cmd/agent/join_test.go).

**Discovery is off by default:** ordinary operations never browse or advertise on the LAN. Explicit discovery finds candidates only; it neither trusts nor enrolls them. Advertisement requires an explicit agent flag and a bounded window. `NSELF_CI_DISCOVERY=0` or user configuration `ci.discovery: off` disables even explicit discovery. With neither switch set, an explicit browse is allowed. A discovered name or fingerprint is a hint, not proof of identity. Pair using a known address when multicast is unavailable. See [discovery guard tests](../../../../free/ci/internal/discovery/guard_test.go) and [spoofing tests](../../../../free/ci/internal/discovery/spoof_test.go).

**Laptops and reservations.** Reserve CPU and memory for the operator, protect interactive sessions, pause or drain on battery, and mark sleeping laptops intermittent. CPU reservations accept cores or a percentage; memory reservations accept MB or GB. These are scheduler reservations, not DHCP leases. For an enrolled `lap1`, `nself ci nodes set lap1 --reserve-cpu 50% --json` is the successful reservation example in [TestNodesRemoteAdminRevokesWithChainedAudit](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_remote_test.go). Other controls are `--reserve-mem`, `--interactive protect`, `--on-battery pause` or `drain`, and `--persistence intermittent`; see [their definitions](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_set.go).

Keep an always-on home-lab box available for jobs that must finish while laptops sleep. A DHCP reservation or stable SSH alias helps reachability; it does not replace key verification or guarantee that a job lease survives sleep. User-mode Linux nodes without working UID separation remain owner-only and cannot gain signing or secret eligibility by advertising capabilities. See [separation tests](../../../../free/ci/internal/nodes/lifecycle/add_test.go).

## VPS

**Host keys and forced SSH options.** Use the same add flow for a dedicated VPS. If using an IP instead of an SSH alias, substitute an example address such as `203.0.113.20`. Verify the destination machine's key even through a jump host. A missing or changed pin stops the connection before job execution.

The SSH carrier forces `BatchMode=yes` and `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`, disables TTY allocation, agent and X11 forwarding, clears forwarding rules, and disables local commands, remote commands, and connection multiplexing. It uses a node-specific host-key alias and the coordinator's pinned known-hosts file. Global known hosts, DNS host-key verification, and known-hosts commands cannot replace that pin. An explicitly supplied identity also uses `IdentitiesOnly=yes`. Do not weaken these settings or discard the user known-hosts file. The exact forced options are checked by [TestSSHTransportForcesOptionSetAndPin](../../../../free/ci/internal/transport/ssh/run_test.go).

**Provisioning versus bootstrap.** `nodes provision` installs self-hosted GitHub Actions runners, dependencies, service users, sudoers configuration, and runner instances. It requires a repository or organization URL and a registration token supplied privately, including through `GITHUB_RUNNER_TOKEN`. The runner download is pinned and checksum-checked. Provisioning records a provider node with unset trust acceptance and `eligible: false`; it does not enroll an eligible native agent. See [provisioning tests](../../../../free/ci/internal/nodes/provision/) and [TestProvisionedRunnerShowsInNodesListWithNullAccepts](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_provision_v15_test.go).

Native agent system bootstrap belongs to `nodes add --system`, not a separate bootstrap subcommand. Supply a trusted agent binary and connect as root or a user with passwordless sudo. Bootstrap creates the agent user, per-slot job users, and restricted job-shim sudoers rules. The landed installer still records this layout as **not UID-separated** until jobs actually use the shim; installation alone grants no secret or signing rights. See [TestSystemInstallBootstrapsAndKeepsTheNodeUnseparated](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_bootstrap_test.go) and [macOS bootstrap tests](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_bootstrap_macos_test.go).

**Deploy hosts are ineligible.** A machine serving deployed applications is outside the normal CI pool because jobs could reach production state and credentials. Inventory checks and agent start guards enforce that boundary. An administrator's explicitly confirmed override permits only owner/internal work with VM isolation or stronger, no release/deploy secrets, and audited placement. Use another machine for CI. See [deploy-host tests](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_override_test.go) and [production boundary rules](../../../../free/ci/internal/trust/prodboundary.go).

## Team

**Personal-nodes rule and `--team`.** A personal coordinator is for the operator's own nodes and work. An unseparated personal node is not a shared team runner; the owner-only personal exception does not carry into team mode. Once anyone other than the operator holds a grant, token, or certificate, start the coordinator with `--team`. This is a boolean flag on `nself ci serve`, not a team-name argument on node commands. The switch is permanent for that data directory and audited; omitting the flag later cannot restore personal mode. See [coordinator mode tests](../../../../free/ci/internal/coordinator/mode/mode_test.go).

**Coordinator-host rule, TRUST D28.** In team mode, any job on the coordinator machine needs VM isolation or stronger. On a personal coordinator, collaborator and untrusted jobs have the same floor; the operator's owner/internal jobs retain their normal minimums. A container alone does not meet the VM floor. Prefer two boxes: keep coordinator state and keys on one, and execute jobs on a separate runner. See [D28 admission](../../../../free/ci/internal/trust/prodboundary.go) and [placement tests](../../../../free/ci/internal/coordinator/mode/floor_test.go).

**Coordinator ports and pairing.** Port 3845 handles webhooks, triggers, and health checks and defaults to loopback. Port 3864 is the agent mTLS listener (`--agent-addr`). Port 3865 is the user API (`--api-addr`), defaulting to loopback, with TLS user certificates or scoped tokens; a Unix socket is also supported. Expose only intended interfaces and use an appropriate TLS endpoint where required. Enrollment has its own listener and pairing window, separate from the user API and agent session. See [agent listener tests](../../../../free/ci/cmd/serve_agent_listener_test.go), [user API implementation](../../../../free/ci/cmd/serve_user_listener.go), and [enrollment tests](../../../../free/ci/cmd/serve_enroll_listener_test.go).

Run add and pair on the coordinator host. They are refused with remote `--coordinator`; that flag cannot move an interactive enrollment flow across the user API. Confirm fingerprints as described under LAN, then restrict accepted work and authorized projects.

**Remote administration and drain.** Select the user API explicitly with `--coordinator <url>` on supported node commands. Configure its trusted root (`ci.coordinator_ca`) and use a user certificate or scoped token with the required project role. Members can list and show nodes; administrative changes require an admin. Without the flag, node commands stay local even if a coordinator is configured for runs. Data-directory access is administrative access. See [remote node tests](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_remote_test.go).

For enrolled `lap1`, the tested maintenance sequence is `nself ci nodes drain lap1 --json`, then `nself ci nodes enable lap1` after maintenance. Add `--coordinator <url>` to send either operation to the remote user API. Drain stops new leases; let active work finish before shutting down. These commands are exercised by [TestNodesRemoteAdminRevokesWithChainedAudit](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_remote_test.go).

**Backup/restore and the KEK.** [TestBackupRestoreCommandsRoundTrip](../../../../free/ci/cmd/serve_backup_test.go) exercises `nself ci serve backup --data-dir <source-dir> --out <archive> --json` and `nself ci serve restore --data-dir <destination-dir> --in <archive> --kek <saved-kek-file> --json`. Stop the destination coordinator before restore. Keep the source coordinator's key-encryption key (KEK) securely and separately: the archive deliberately excludes it, and a wrong KEK is refused before state is written. The archive alone cannot recover sealed key material.

Restore verifies the archive, preserves existing revocations and deny-list entries, advances the incarnation, and rotates token signing keys. An empty-directory restore marks nodes `needs-reconfirm`; verify each before enabling it. Retain the saved previous state and rollback instructions until healthy. See [restore behavior](../../../../free/ci/cmd/serve_backup.go).

**Rotation and revocation.** For a paired node, `nself ci nodes rotate node-pull --cert` denies its existing certificates; re-pair using the pinned node key for a fresh certificate. Node-key rotation explicitly supplies the replacement key ID and differs from SSH host-key rotation. Revocation denies certificates and expires leases. Certificate rotation and re-pairing cannot recover a revoked identity. See [rotation and revocation tests](../../../../free/ci/cmd/nodes_pair_test.go).

**Upgrades.** Upgrade the coordinator before agents when the protocol ceiling requires it. Agent upgrades verify signed artifacts, drain and wait for jobs, swap atomically, and restore the previous drain state. Fleet upgrades proceed sequentially and stop at the first failure. An administrator's intentional drain remains in place. Do not bypass signature checks or assume an unpinned release exists. Consult the generated [version reference](./Reference.md#pinned-versions) and [upgrade tests](../../../../free/ci/internal/agent/update/).

## Troubleshooting

Start with `nself ci doctor --nodes --json`, exercised by [TestNodesSection](../../../../free/ci/cmd/doctor_nodes_test.go). Match the subject and remediation to the generated [CI-DN doctor-check table](./Reference.md#doctor-checks). For E650–E669 and reason keys, use the generated [error-code table](./Reference.md#error-codes). Reference.md owns these tables; this guide does not copy them or invent per-row anchors.

**Lost leases.** Sleep, a dropped SSH session, or coordinator outage can end a lease. Restore connectivity, inspect the attempt, and let fencing and cleanup finish before retrying. Expired leases can leave orphan job roots; restarting the agent sweeps roots whose leases are gone. A stale epoch must not resume the old job. Check disk space, time synchronization, battery policy, and intermittent-node settings. Discovery does not renew leases. See [state diagnostics](../../../../free/ci/internal/nodes/doctor/checks_state.go) and [session-drop tests](../../../../free/ci/internal/transport/ssh/run_test.go).

**Host-key change.** Verify the replacement fingerprint out of band, then rotate the SSH pin using `nodes rotate` with `--host-key`. Do not disable strict checking or re-bootstrap merely to silence the error. A changed node signing key or expired certificate is a different identity problem; follow its reported remediation and pairing/rotation flow. See [host-key rotation tests](../../../../free/ci/internal/nodes/lifecycle/integration_test.go).

**No eligible runner.** Check whether the node is drained, revoked, a deploy host, unauthorized for the project, below the required isolation, or missing UID separation for team use. A provisioned GitHub runner in the inventory is not automatically an eligible native agent. Consult the generated tables before changing trust and use [Trust, Security, and Privacy](./Trust-Security-and-Privacy.md) for admission policy.
